What the caller could do now (U2): a hint; on a write's answer it
is decided on the facts read before the lock.

(`forge_auth::MergeSettingsViewer`) — a hint for the screen, never a

current ones: `status` says `unchecked` until the next check.

`unchecked`, `checking`, `can_be_merged`, `cannot_be_merged` or

its old path. Each keeps that path blocked until released; a clone
or fetch through it is redirected (`302`) to the new path for
callers who may read the project, a push through it is refused.

oneOf.description: M3 R6: the rule's merge conditions (`null`: none).

The minimum role that may push (create / fast-forward) a matching
ref; force-push and deletion are refused for everyone.

M3 C1: the required checks behind `required_checks_unreportable`
(empty without the warning). Only in a merge-rule write's answer.

Things to know about the answer (M3 R6 review). M3 I1d:
`work_item_link_unbound` — the merge rule requires a work item link
and the project has no integration binding, so no merge request can
satisfy it (bind the project, or turn the condition off; runbook
merge-blocked). `required_checks_unreportable` (M3 C1: narrowed): the merge rule
requires a check no active service account may report (its
namespace is granted to none, or it is `forge/`, whose own checks
arrive later), so every merge into the branch is blocked
(`required_check_missing`); with the direct-push ban the branch
cannot change at all. The names are in `unreportable_checks`. Grant
the namespace to a service account, or remove the check names
(runbooks checks-reporting, merge-blocked). Empty otherwise.

string), or `null` to create a rule no rule has the name of.

removed, or created by someone else — is FG-REVIEW-0018 and nothing
is written.

comes back by itself at the expiry).

expected_updated_at.description:
The merge rule's `updated_at` the caller read, echoed verbatim (an
opaque string), or `null` when the branch has none (create only).
Required (U2 follow-up): another merge rule under the lock — changed,
removed, or created by someone else — is FG-REVIEW-0019 and nothing
is written.

require_resolved_discussions.description: Every discussion of the merge request must be resolved.

M3 I1d: a merge request merges only with an open link to a work item
of the project's integration binding (`work_item_link_missing`). On
a project without a binding the answer warns
`work_item_link_unbound`. Required (I1d review): a client that does
not know the field must not turn the condition off by leaving it out
(FG-WEB-0006 `reason=missing_field`).

required_approvals.description: The minimum counted approvals of a merge into the branch, 0..=20.

Checks that must have succeeded on the merge request's head, at
most 20, each `ci/…`, `kanflow/…` or `forge/…` (`ext/…` is refused,

(never round-tripped through a date type: it is to the microsecond)
— or `null` for the defaults, never stored. Required (U2): another
value under the lock is FG-REVIEW-0017 — the settings changed in
between and nothing is overwritten silently.

revoked_sessions.description: How many sessions ended (0: there were none).

body.description: The first note: plain text / Markdown, 1 character to 60 KiB.

oneOf.description: Absent: a general discussion on the merge request.

StatusApprovalBody.description: One live approval as counted now.

codeowners.description: CODEOWNERS rules the changed paths need: `pattern`, satisfied.

StatusCheckBody.description: One required check and its run on the head.

StatusCodeownerBody.description: One CODEOWNERS rule the changes need.

suspended_until.description: While suspended: when enforcement comes back by itself (UTC).

detail.description:
`key=value` pairs (`rule=… required=… counted=…`, `name=…`,
`count=…`, …); `null` for the plain reasons.

StatusReasonName.description:
The name of a blocking reason (ADR-0024 §7): one per
`forge_review::BlockReason` variant, spelled as `BlockReason::as_str`
(`status_reason_schema_lists_every_block_reason`). A new reason is a
new name here — added, never renamed, within `schema_version` 1.

StatusRuleBody.description: One approval requirement (an approval rule, or `@protected_branch`).

StatusViewerBody.description:
What the caller could do now (U2): each flag is `authorize()` on the
context the action's route decides on (`forge_auth::MergeRequestViewer`)
— a hint for the screen, never a permission (the route decides again).

approved_by_me.description: The caller has a live approval of the merge request.

can_approve.description: `POST …/approve` would be allowed (never for the author).

can_mark_ready.description:
`PATCH …/{iid}` with `draft: false` would be allowed (meaningful
only for a draft).

can_merge.description:
`POST …/merge` would be allowed (the target's minimum push role;
whether the merge request may merge now is `mergeable`).

can_unapprove.description:
`POST …/unapprove` would be allowed (pair it with `approved_by_me`:
there may be nothing to withdraw).

StatusWorkItemLinkBody.description: The work item link condition (M3 I1d).

linked.description:
An open link to a work item of the project's integration binding
exists (`false`: `work_item_link_missing`).

TokenBody.description: One token as the API shows it (never the secret or its hash).

namespace_id.description:
The new parent group's `namespace_id`. Omitted: the current parent
(a rename; a top-level group stays at the top level).

path.description: The new last segment. Omitted: the current one.

reclaim.description: As for a project: take back an old path of this group's subtree.

top_level.description:
`true`: move to the top level (administrators only); not together
with `namespace_id`.

namespace_id.description:
The new parent: a group or a personal namespace (`namespace_id` of
`GET /api/v1/groups/{id}`, of a user, or of the resolver). Omitted:
the current parent (a rename).

path.description: The new last segment (ADR-0015 rules). Omitted: the current one.

reclaim.description:
Take back an old path of this very project (A → B → A): release, in
the same change, the `moved` tombstone there that names it. Default
`false` (a tombstone always blocks until released).

entries.description: In git's order (byte order of the names).

path.description: The tree's path (`""` for the root).

truncated.description: More entries than the server lists (5 000).

draft.description:
Only the author or a Maintainer changes another's flag; only while
open.

target_branch.description: A branch other than the source; it must exist; only while open.

owner_id.description: A new owner (an active human user's id): offboarding hands it on.

enabled.description: `true` enables it again and clears its failure count.

UserNameBody.description: A user as the merge request screens name them (MR B0).

UserSelf.description: The caller's account as the API shows it.

is_agent.description: The credential is a token issued for an AI agent.

token_scopes.description: The token's scopes; `null` for a session.

VersionBody.description: One version of a merge request.

base_sha.description:
The target's tip when the version was recorded (`null` until the
version job recorded it, or when the target was missing).

merge_base_sha.description:
The merge base of the head and `base_sha` (`null`: not recorded, or
no common history). The version's diff starts here.

pushed_by.description:
The pusher whose push made the version (`null` for the first
version of a new or reopened merge request).

refs_purged.description:
The version's refs were removed (secret removal): its diff is no
longer served.

commits.description: The commits `to` has and `from` does not, newest first.
The commits `to` has and `from` does not, newest first.

commits_truncated.description: More commits than the server lists (200).

from.description:
The commit the diff starts at: `merge_base_sha`, or `base_sha` when
there was no common history.

already_purged.description: Versions purged before (their refs were removed again if present).

purged.description: Versions marked and whose refs were removed by this request.

VersionsBody.description: A merge request's versions, oldest first.

VisibilityName.description: A project's visibility in a request.

disabled_reason.description: `manual`, `failures` (50 failed attempts in a row) or `failing_24h`.

origin.description:
`scheme://host:port` of the URL. The full URL is write-only: its
path or query may hold the receiver's token (I2 review).

owner_id.description:
The person who answers for it: who created it, or last changed its
URL or event types or rotated its secret. Deliveries stop when they
can no longer manage the project's webhooks.

previous_secret_valid_until.description: The previous secret still signs until then (UTC, RFC 3339).

secret_version.description: The version of the current secret (`Forge-Signature-Kid`).

WorkItemBody.description: A work item as kanflow names it (02 §5.7's `work_items` entry).

project_id.description: The external (kanflow) project of the binding.

outcome.description:
`linked` (also when a detected link became the person's) or
`unchanged` (already linked by hand).

source.description: `auto` or `manual`: how the (found) link was made.

linked_by.description: Who linked it by hand (`null` for a detected link).

source.description: `auto` (detected in the title or the source branch) or `manual`.

unlink_source.description:
`auto` (the title no longer names it), `manual`, `converted` (a
person linked the detected work item: their link follows) or
`unbound` (the project was unbound); `null` while open.

unlinked_by_kind.description:
`human`, `agent`, `service_account` or `bot`; only a `human`'s
`manual` unlink keeps detection from linking it again.
